function: Pretrained DDPG outputs BS information and energy precoders, STAR-RIS transmission/reflection coefficients and RSMA common-rate allocation to maximize worst-case secrecy rate under imperfect eavesdropper CSI (p. 6).
system: MISO downlink, N_T=4 BS antennas, STAR-RIS with M=10 elements, K=J=2 information and untrusted energy receivers, RSMA, SWIPT; narrow-band Rician channels; no carrier frequency stated (pp. 3, 7).
method: Unsupervised-pretrained DDPG: pseudo-actor and pseudo-critic pretrained on random states to maximize the immediate reward, then transferred to DDPG; two-hidden-layer fully connected networks (pp. 6-7).
data_channel: Custom simulator: narrow-band quasi-static Rician fading for BS-RIS and RIS-user links (K=3 dB, path-loss exponent 2.2) with Rayleigh NLoS; no standard model or dataset (p. 7).
test_conditions: Averaged over 100 independent evaluation episodes of trained policies; sweeps over transmit power, antennas, STAR-RIS elements and same-side deployment; no unseen-condition test stated (pp. 7-8).
baselines: Non-learned: SPCA-FIPSA of [12] (legend: Algorithms 1 and 4 in [18]). Learned: DDPG and PPO (Fig. 3), DDPG and TD3 (Fig. 4) (pp. 7-8).
metrics: Sum secrecy rate versus transmit power, antennas and STAR-RIS elements; minimum secrecy rate; reward versus episode (convergence speed) (pp. 7-8).
q1_support: p. 7: "are modeled using Rician fading channels as follows [18]". Custom narrow-band Rician and Rayleigh simulator with a simple path-loss law; no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 7: "All results are averaged over 100 independent evaluation episodes using the trained policies". Fig. 2(a)-(b) (p. 8) plots secrecy rate against training steps with one curve per antenna or element count; no statement that a trained model is tested in an unseen scenario, size or band.
q3_support: p. 7: "the conventional DRL baselines using their tuned hyperparameters". Fig. 3 (p. 8) plots sum secrecy rate against transmit power for the optimization benchmark (SPCA-FIPSA of [12]), DDPG and PPO; Fig. 4 compares reward with DDPG and TD3.
q4_support: p. 7: "the trained UP-DDPG policy directly generates resource-allocation decisions". Only qualitative statements; no order of complexity, operations, parameters (hidden size H is not given, p. 6) or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 6: "trained using a randomly generated state dataset". Pretraining and evaluation use simulated data; the paper gives no code or data link, public dataset or measurement.
notes: The version given is preprint; the PDF is the accepted author manuscript (pages 1-2 are the repository cover and rights pages, the article starts on page 3). Area 3: the learned part sets precoders and STAR-RIS coefficients, and secrecy rate is only the design objective. Figure legends were read from the rendered page 8. The Fig. 3 legend cites Algorithm 4 and Algorithm 1 in [18] for the optimization benchmarks while the text names SPCA-FIPSA of [12]; the citation is inconsistent in the paper. The DDPG baseline is UP-DDPG without pretraining, so PPO and TD3 are the learned baselines that count for q3.
